text_fidelity_a:
Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome I figured the Fisher-Price Power Wheels Dune Racer would be a great way to keep my nieces' occupied when they visit. It certainly made them very happy when they saw it! Over all, it's a great power cart and an improvement on the one they have at home, but there are one or two minor issues.
It was delivered in a large box, and since is a 'some assembly required' type of toy, some components were not secured in the box. These parts were in plastic packed within thin foam, along with heavier parts, and had been bounced around in shipping. Because of the way the racer was packed, this meant that there were some scratches on some of the smaller chromed plastic pieces. A minor detail, but some people might not be happy to have a toy arrive in less than pristine shape (also, know that a VERY large box may be just left on your porch or by your garage).
Assembly took the boyfriend about 45 minutes using a screw gun with no issues... but he's pretty good about putting things together. Might take some others a bit longer.
While we tested the battery and found out that it had a little charge right out of the box, for a full charge, you pretty much will have to charge it overnight (about eighteen hours). So yeah, there's a bit of delayed fun-time with the toy. Might be some disappointed kiddies if they see it and then find out they can't do much more than sit in it for about a day.
The decals were tough to peel from the sheet. The wax paper was peeling off along with the sticker due to how thin the stickers were, and they were cut too deep into the backing paper. All in all they were a bit of a pain to put onto the racer - might not be worth it to put them on at all (not sure my nieces care about them, to be honest).
Another minor issue is that the gas pedal is in the middle of the cart, causing the driver to stretch a little to reach (especially when you add that you can't move the seat forward). The shifter was also in the center, as well as directly under the driver’s right knee (at least for my nieces, who are a little more than four years old). So when they were touching the gas pedal, it would sometime shift gears on them, between reverse, low and high. They seem to be learning to be more careful, but still, something to be concerned about when this happened, especially in reverse when they would hit the gas, and their leg would bump the shifter into forwards, causing the cart to lurch in that direction.
A nice thing about the Fisher-Price racer is that it goes well on both grass and on hills with a 30 degree angle. Compared to an older power wheels toddler 6v that the girls have that couldn't manage going up hills, they're having so much more fun (and want to take it home). The seat is comfortable and the racer looks great (scratches aside).
There is no 'brake' to the racer, but once the foot is removed from the gas pedal, it stops.
All in all, the racer is a hit and I'm sure the girls will be begging to come over to use it. One or two features could be better designed (I have to wonder if it's to fit to older kids as well to younger), but on the whole, it's a very nice cart that kids should be able to enjoy for a couple of years (depending on their age).
Overall the kids love it and have a blast with it. Giving 4 stars because of packing, QC issues, and some ergo issues.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

Bobby Fischer® Learn to Play Chess Set Board Game, Easy to Understand - How to Play Chess Book, 34 Plastic Staunton Chess Pieces, Folding Illustrated Chess Board, Family Games for Kids and Adults When I was in middle school, a teacher I did not really know invited me in to learn chess. It changed my life. I wanted to pass the information on to my kids, but it was hard to get them to make connections. This set is great.

WHAT IS THIS SET LIKE?
This set comes with a four fold board, big sized pieces, general instructions, and two dice.

BOARD
The board has information right on it, so that you don't have to repeat it over and over for visual learners.

PIECES
The pieces in this box are plenty big enough, have a nice felt bottom and are all in the box. Nothing was missing. There were even the two extra queens in the box too.

IS IT EASY TO TEACH WITH?
I found that this is really easy to teach with and in my case, it has been a while since I could play chess with someone and not a computer, so I found this very exciting.

DICE
The dice is a great way to even out playing with a beginner which helps a lot because who wants to be beaten constantly?

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great set for a beginner chess learner. The board is small, the pieces easy to use and the directions clear and well laid out. The dice make it fun for mis matched players (beginner vs more advanced).

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like this set and am glad to have it. My family is finally going to learn chess without me having to continually explain everything. The visuals are great.
text_fidelity_b: Bobby Fischer® Learn to Play Chess Set Board Game, Easy to Understand - How to Play Chess Book, 34 Plastic Staunton Chess Pieces, Folding Illustrated Chess Board, Family Games for Kids and Adults

This isn’t a set for young kids, unless they are closely supervised while building. I’d say adults and older teens, due to the small size of the pieces and complexity of the instructions.

Unlike most building sets where the pieces for each step are shown next to that step, these instructions show a bunch of pieces for several steps at once. So you might have a pile of 50 or 60 pieces for the next 3 or 4 steps (or more).

The instructions themselves require attention to detail, you really have to pay attention to how the pieces are laid out. A single step might involve 20 pieces or more.

Instructions aside, the pieces don’t snap together very well. I was building the ship on a desk, but even with the hard surface, the pieces aren’t straight. The bottom of my Titanic is curling upwards even before I get to the part that’s supposed to be bent from the iceberg. I pressed so hard my fingers hurt but I still couldn’t get all the pieces to fit together as they should.

I wish the stand for the bottle was made from bricks instead of faux wood. The stand looks clunky and is flimsy.

text_fidelity_a:
GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa Impressive shower head at an impressive price. Let's break it down...

** IN THE BOX ** Along with the showerhead there is a small roll of teflon thread tape, rubber pipe gasket, in-pipe flow restrictor, and instructions.

** INSTALLATION ** Remove old shower head. Clean pipe threads. Apply 3 turns of pipe thread in a CLOCKWISE direction. Extend shower head extension pipe arm all the way out. If you want flow restriction, insert now, other insert pipe gasket. Attach shower head in a CLOCKWISE direction by hand until tight. Cover the plastic thread cap (nearest the pipe) with a cloth and tighten 1/4 turn with a pliers or pipe wrench using GENTLE pressure. The shower head can now be straightened by gentle turning the adjustment screw (nearest shower head) by hand. It will click. Once you have the general downward direction of the shower head placed, test for leaks. If it leaks at the pipe & shower head connection, gently tighten another 1/4 turn. Once you're ready you can position the shower head, by head, any which way you like . It will click letting you know it's locked.

** USAGE ** Turn water on to your favorite temperature and insert your glorious naked self under the shower head. Look up at the nipples. Yes, there are 90 nipples up there. Very supple nipples that can be squeezed for cleaning. With so many nipples I don't think I'm ever leaving the shower ever again. The 90 nipples provided me an even pressurized rain all over my smelly carcass.

** THOUGHTS ** The TH2.5 works like a charm. Big, even rain all over me. Just what I wanted. Installation was simple provided you have normal shower pipes and are a bit handy with some pliers. The joints articulate well with no movement once set. The joints, once set, should accommodate short and tall humans. I'm 6'1", the wild redhead is 5'7" so this head works amazingly well for both of us. Did I mention there were 90 nipples?

** POINTS OF INTEREST **
- flow is optional and NOT installed
- joints articulate with a solid 'click' and stay in place
- pipe tape and gasket are included
- cover with cloth during final tightening to avoid scratching
- gently squeeze the nipples to clean
- looks like the USS Enterprise from the side... Aye, Aye Captain!
- I just love saying the word 'nipples'
text_fidelity_b: GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa

Rainbow Loom® Treasure Box NEON Edition, 8,000 Rubber Bands in 8 Different Neon Colors, and a BONUS of 2 Happy Looms, Great Activities for Boys and Girls 7+ I have the Sparkles Treasure Box from Rainbow Loom. For the original maker, I expected much better quality.

Every single color had broken bands. I know bands can break, but I shouldn’t encounter broken ones within the first handful I pull from each bag. And I had to redo bracelets twice because bands broke in the middle of the bracelet, so the bracelet came apart. I’ve tried no-name loom bands and had zero breakage, so that’s really disappointing that the actual Rainbow Loom ones broke.

For a pack called “Sparkles” I expected that every color would be glittery. Nope. Only three of the colors are glittery: clear, green, and violet purple (dark purple). The other five are pearly: gold, pink, lilac purple (light purple), sky blue (light blue), and blue (dark blue).

On the plus side, the box includes 2 Happy Looms and step-by-step picture instructions for making a fishtail bracelet. I was able to find a lot of video tutorials by looking for “2 peg” bracelets, too.

text_fidelity_a:
Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game Lexicon Go is a very fast-paced, easy-to-play word game using a deck of 52 plastic tiles, each with a letter of the alphabet. the tiles are arranged face down on the playing area, and each player draws 10 tiles from the deck. The goal is to arrange all 10 of your tiles into words as quickly as possible. If you're unable to use all of your letters to make words, you can swap out a tile (within certain parameters) or you can play on other players' words. The first player to use all 10 tiles wins the round. Win five rounds and you've won the game.

We played this game with two, three, four, and five adult players. I would guess that in at least 8 out of 10 rounds, one player was able to use all of her letters to form words without any swapping out or playing on another player's tiles -- which made the game move very, very quickly, , but also made it a little bit boring. There is very little strategizing and interaction. The best part was challenging words and learning the meaning of funny new words.

This was a little bit too fast-paced and frenetic for my tastes, and whether you could use all your tiles on the first draw depended primarily on getting a good vowel to consonant ratio- if you draw at least three vowels, it's pretty easy to make two, three, or four letter words to use all ten tiles. If you draw only one or two vowels, you will have a tough time using all your tiles.

The game is fun, clever, and well-made. The carrying case is well-made and the tiles are nice quality. This would be a great family game or vacation game, and it worked equally well with two players as it did with five players -- it just worked differently. It is versatile. If you're a fan of Scrabble or the New York Times crossword, this seems very fast-paced and a little too easy. It may better suited for younger players -- maybe elementary school-aged children.
text_fidelity_b: Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game

LEGO City Race Boat Transporter 60254 Race Boat Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (238 Pieces) This LEGO CITY RACE BOAT TRANSPORTER BUILDING SET ((60254) New 2020, 238 Pieces) is fairly easy to build--the difficulty is what I’d call “normal” for a City-themed set. City sets are among my favorites, because they include fire trucks, police stations, buses, trains, beachgoer minifigs, space stations, and all the rest of the things that a bustling city (or the airspace above it) needs. This particular set is aimed at ages 5 and up.

The set contains all the pieces required to build three separate items: a semi-trailer truck (for towing the race boat), a trailer for hauling the race boat, and a race boat. (You can use the truck’s trailer hitch to tow other things that you build, of course.)

The “Xtreme” graphics are NOT printed on the pieces, but are applied with stickers. (I hate stickers, too.) Applying stickers is made easier if you first stick a corner to something long and thin (e.g., a spudger or a plastic knife) so that you can better control the placement on the element. A good thing about LEGO stickers is that they can be removed and replaced (like Post-Its) if you get them misaligned.

The LEGO elements are compatible with other City sets and with all regular LEGO sets (but not with DUPLO sets, which have extra-large pieces for very young builders). The Race Boat Transporter set is another fine addition to the extensive collection of City sets.

You build parks and enclosures to house dinosaurs. The dinosaurs are hungry. If you can't feed them, they'll still eat - guess what? - your other dinosaurs! Very well made and lots of fun. If you don't like this game, maybe board games aren't your thing.

I look at this game as an example to understand how to make games well. I think anyone who likes board games has to give at least one Tiny Epic game a try, and this is the one I would recommend most.

Limited closet space? Desperate for something besides Monopoly, Risk, or Settlers of Catan? Like building games with dire consequences? Think dinosaurs are the least bit cool or interesting? Look no further.

My only minor criticism is that some might consider it complex with the different special dinosaurs and some of the rules about how and when to place dinos. Any board game is going to have a learning curve, and this one is small.

AniBlock Puzzle Challenger Lite I Brain Game and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 4 and 5 This was delivered to my house about an hour ago, and my 6 year old daughter is about to put it away. She's just now finishing up the hardest puzzle included in the kit.

I'm torn on how to review this. It's clearly a nice toy for a lot of kids. The pieces are nice and chunky, the puzzle cards have vibrant artwork, and the app works smoothly. That said, though, there are 12 puzzle cards in the box, and yes, they can be solved multiple ways, but there is no guidance for different combinations of blocks to use to complete the puzzles, so there isn't much incentive to take them off and try again. Also, for someone who is not too far removed from the minimum age range suggested though, it's really easy. Like, a puzzle in two minutes for almost every combo in the deck, except for the boat, which is in the middle of the difficulty spectrum. On the box, with an oddly small top, there are images of three-dimensional shapes made out of the aniblocks, flying around, and the actual blocks do not connect in this way to form them, which was probably the most disappointing part.

The app deserves some special mention. It's certainly good, and easy to use, but it's still an app, and so, of course, it defeats the purpose of having a screen avoidant time to include it. There's also another disadvantage, which is that there are tons of apps that do this same game already, with digital blocks. They offer more puzzles, with more diverse colors of blocks, in more diverse shapes, and a wider variety of difficulty levels.

Overall, I think there are better toys for your money that do very similar things and offer a lot more variety than this. The phone apps, as mentioned before. We have a board game called Blokus 3D (or Rumis) which have a similar pattern-matching idea, but allow for 3D building. There's also Kanoodle Junior, for example, which is excellent, cheaper, ready to travel, and doesn't require an app. 12 puzzles and a handful of two-colored blocks is just not enough for the price. For that reason, I cannot recommend this...but there are far worse options.
text_fidelity_b: AniBlock Puzzle Challenger Lite I Brain Game and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 4 and 5

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Crayon Maker with Story Studio Kids love to color, so a toy like the Crayola Crayon Maker would seem like an ideal addition to any home with children under the age of eight. Coloring with your child's own crayons he/she just made would seem like a great creative addition to an already fun activity.

Unfortunately, the fun with this toy stops at the concept itself. Making crayons is a great idea, but this device has several issues that prevent it from living up to its potential. The way it works is simple enough- you place the crayon material on a tray and set a timer. The heat from the lightbulb melts the crayons, which are then poured into a mold. You then wait for them to cool and they are ready to use. This sounds simple, but there are all sorts of problems along the way, and many of them seem to stem from Crayola's desire to apparently make the crayon maker as safe as possible.

One issue is with the locking mechanism. As you move from one step to the next, the device locks itself and you cannot unlock until the cycle is completed. For example, when the crayons are transferred to the molds, there is no way to unlock at this point. You are forced to wait for the crayons to cool before you can open. Issues with the timer are similarly frustrating- if your child accidentally sets the timer prematurely, you have no choice but to wait until it is finished. You cannot move the timer forward. You have to wait for it to complete its cycle.

Another issue I have is with the melting phase. There is no buzzer or anything to tell you that the crayons are ready to transfer to the molds. Thus, you have to pay close attention and make sure you are there, when the light bulb goes off, ready to transfer. If you don't act promptly, the crayons will cool off and solidify in the tray.

These frustrations might be tolerable enough for more patient types, but there is one ultimate frustration is enough to make you want to give up and ask for a refund. I am referring to the amount of crayons included in each package. You get only enough to make two crayons! You heard me correctly- two small crayons! When you consider what you have to go through just to get a pair of crayons and when you consider how inexpensive crayons are, it makes you wonder why you even bothered to obtain this device in the first place.

Making crayons can be fun and there are many ways to make them using ordinary household heat sources, utensils, etc. I recommend making crayons the old fashioned way and skipping the Crayola Crayon Maker completely. It is a good idea gone bad and I can only hope that Crayola has a new and improved version in the making.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Crayon Maker with Story Studio

fansmart 39" Pull -Along Wagon for Kids with Pulling Wood Railing Panels Outdoor Wagon 10" All Terrain Air Tires 330 lbs Capacity for Beach, Garden, Sporting Events, Park（Red） I got this 'Lil Red Wagon' from Fansmart mainly for around the house use. I have a much MUCH larger garden wagon that can be pulled by hand or hooked up to your lawn and garden mower/tractor. But, it's just not convenient for doing simple things around the flower garden. This Fansmart wagon is great for that. Putting it together, I noted a few things. 1) Don't overtighten the acorn nuts. You will pop the caps right off. 2) The wood stake and slate side panels are NOT the most solidly built. The wood is soft pine and the panels are just stapled together. My advice would be to coat them very well with some clear polyurethane or other wood preservative before assembly. And, don't be too rough or careless when working with them. it's okay to put a load against them. Jut understand that there are limitations on how much abuse they can take. 3) When putting the cotter pins through the axles, to hold the wheels on, make sure you bend them all the way around the axles, to prevent any chance of a puncture or laceration from the sharp ends of the cotter pins. 4) Use your common sense in assembling the front yoke / truck assembly. The illustration is not that detailed. But, it's fairly simple. The finished front end will NOT be that tightly fitted when you're done. That's okay. It's the way it was designed. 5) The rounded pan head of all the bolts going through the pan of the wagon go ON THE INSIDE of the pan, not the outside. Even then, the heads do not seat perfectly into the holes. They do have an edge that can snag on bagged materials like mulch, potting soil, etc. My advice would be to lay a piece of cardboard or something in the bed of the wagon. The would both prevent tears in your bagged materials AND protect the finish of the wagon.

I've been using mine for hauling heavy plants around and even moving frozen goods from the deep freeze to the snow bank, during this 'winter storm of the century' that we had down here in Texas. The power was out for four days and I didn't want to lose roughly $700 in venison. Lil Red did the trick.

If anyone is old enough to remember the 'Radio Flyer' wagons that were sold a few decades ago, this wagon is kind of like that. But, not as big and not as heavily constructed. However, this wagon is good enough quality, for the price, to still earn a five star rating from me.
text_fidelity_b: fansmart 39" Pull -Along Wagon for Kids with Pulling Wood Railing Panels Outdoor Wagon 10" All Terrain Air Tires 330 lbs Capacity for Beach, Garden, Sporting Events, Park（Red）

Retro Handheld Game Console, Portable Video Game Console with 400 Classical 8 Bit FC Games 2.8 Inch Screen 1020MAh Rechargeable Battery Support Connecting TV (Blue) I love the old console games and I looked to this handheld to revisit some of the older games I remember enjoying several years ago. For the price this is a decent little console and I like it, though there is some room for improvement.

In the past, playing the older games required downloading a ROM and putting it into an emulator, and if you knew where to look for ROMs you could find hundreds of them, many familiar and even more that were very unfamiliar. I expected this little console to be something silimar to the old emulator, preloaded with old ROMs, and it seems to be fairly close to that. There are many games I recognize that are a lot fo fun to revisit, and there are a lot of games that are unfamiliar.

This console comes preloaded with several hundred games of varying types and quality. As mentioned there are quite a few that are familiar, but many that I never saw in an arcade. Some appear to be Asian releases that never were released here.

Navigation is a minor pain. If you want to play a game that is far down the list, you have to navigate there every time. There doesn't appear to be any memory for last games played.

Another minor disappointment is that several titles are listed more than once in the menu. This suggests to me that there are different versions, even if I can't tell what the differences are.

I'm thinking this is the same thing as the old emulators that can be found online and it just packaged in a handheld and preloaded with ROMs. That's fine by me, I like those old games. It would have been nice to provide better navigation, though, and maybe reduce the versions of each game to the latest or most bug-free? For the cost, it's a worthwhile system if you love those old games.
text_fidelity_b: Retro Handheld Game Console, Portable Video Game Console with 400 Classical 8 Bit FC Games 2.8 Inch Screen 1020MAh Rechargeable Battery Support Connecting TV (Blue)

Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+ We absolutely love our dinosaurs, dragons, and lifelike statues of real animals from this brand, and this extra-large dinosaur is no exception. The thing you should know about these is that they are a very hard resin like material. This makes them much better for children who are old enough to use the statues responsibly and not bash them on things such as their little sister, because they are very hard and heavy and have absolutely no give to them. On this particular model, the end of the tail is the most dangerous part aside from the sheer size and weight of the overall piece.

This dinosaur is much larger than the cheapo dinosaurs that you get in multi-packs that are made in China, and the level of craftsmanship and detail here is sufficient for even the most exacting dinosaur connoisseur. That said, though the description talks about scoop shaped teeth being a major part of what makes this dinosaur cool, I was unable to really discern much scoop detail on the teeth, given the relative size of the teeth versus the relative size of the dinosaur. Just something to be aware of. But that's not me complaining about the level of detail.

I love the artistic detailing on the hide, the bluish bumps on the back, the little spines, and the huge amount of expression in the face. My toddler son is just beginning a dinosaur phase and enjoyed stomping this large dinosaur through his truck collection and roaring with great feeling. I think that as his knowledge of dinosaurs expands, so will his appreciation of all the small differentiating details that give this dinosaur personality, character, and most importantly, accuracy.

As long as you are aware of the hard and heavy resin material used to create these, you will be deeply impressed by the detailing, durability, and potential for imaginative play inherent in the figure.

text_fidelity_a:
Logo Party Board Game "Logo Party" gives players the chance to guess famous logos in a variety of ways. Depending on what type of card you draw, you will try to have other players guess the logo by drawing the clues (like Pictionary), acting out the item (as in Charades), or describing the brand (like the old game show "Pyramid".) Players have twenty seconds to guess the brand from the clues provided. Each team has a token to move around the board and try to get to the end first by guessing more brands than the other team. The game includes a tablet for the drawing clues and a box to hold the cards during play and for storage. Unfortunately, the box is too small and the cards don't fit well.

The game is designed for four or more players divided into two teams. The recommended ages are listed as eight and up, but most eight-year-olds would be unfamiliar with many of the brands featured in the game. In fact, even older teens and adults won't know some of these brands. Also, I would call some of the items products and not brands. For example, one of the "brands" is Chicken McNuggets (as opposed to McDonald's.)

The game is somewhat fun, but would be much better with a large group of people. My family found it almost impossible to act out most of the brands, but it was funny to see people try to act things out like "Tupperware". With more people, I'm sure it would be even funnier.

Throughout the boards, there are spaces called, "Reveal It". When landing on this space, players from both teams try to guess a brand by looking at the logo. This is also how the winner is ultimately determined when teams reach the end of the game board. The timer that comes with the game doubles as a holder for these cards. The card starts out fully covered and then parts of the brand are slowly revealed. This is a clever idea, but it's hard to place the card in the holder without looking at. Also, it makes an annoying buzzing sound (like the sound of a small wind-up toy.) Because of the sound, we used a different timer during regular play and saved the timer for the "Reveal It" cards.

The game would be more fun for a large group of people. My family had some fun playing "Logo Party", but got bored after a while since some of the brands were unknown to some of the players and it was hard to act out the brands and actually get someone to guess them.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Party Board Game

Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome This is a fun ride-on toy for kids. I like that it sits close to the ground, which makes it better for younger kids, but the design is still “cool” enough that older kids will still like it. The dune buggy has a lot of good features. First, the blue color will appeal to both girls and boys. The vehicle has two speeds, which is nice. However, the parent lock-out needs to be removed to access the higher speed. The lock-out is a screw that’s fairly difficult to remove because of its location. The higher speed is definitely needed to easily ride in the wet grass, even on flat ground. It’s fairly easy to steer the vehicle and is a lot of fun for kids to drive.

To stop the vehicle, take your foot off the gas pedal. It will still slide a little on pavement, possibly because of the plastic wheels. It also will continue to slowly roll going downhill, even on a small incline. That’s why even though the guidelines say ages 3 to 7, I would use caution for younger kids unless you have a large, flat area with no nearby hills. Older kids, up to 11 or 12, will like it, too. However, with the position of the steering wheel, their height will determine how well they’ll comfortably fit in the dune buggy and be able to easily steer.

Be sure to charge the battery the night before using the first time. The battery only lasted about 15 minutes right out of the box after being putting the car together. I also learned the hard way that the dune buggy is heavy to push if it does bog down or if the battery dies. (The battery is rechargeable battery, but there isn’t a battery indicator, so I wasn’t expecting it to go dead so quickly.)

Once the dune buggy is assembled and the battery is charged, it’s a lot of fun for kids. The assembly is a chore for adults, though. I took almost an hour and a half to assemble. Most of that time was spent putting on the wheels. The directions aren’t clear and some of the screws are hard to get to and there isn’t room to use an electric screwdriver. As long as you allow enough time for assembly and charging the battery, this dune buggy will be a hit.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

As a die hard Star Wars Fan this Saber has a lot going for it, but a few cons. First the build and look are nice. The sound is also very good. The price is one of the best reasons for getting one. For the $72.00 you're getting 12 Light Sabers "colors" compare that to $250.00 and higher for one color. Now for the cons the blade is held in place by three set screws and it still has a bit of a lose feeling not much but its there. The other thing is the control button it is a bit cumbersome and by that I mean the holding down or pushing or doing the fast twist while holding button down to change sound fonts. I know some other saber makers use similar features but not this hard to change. One of the sound fonts is not even from Star Wars. I did not know what it was and could not stand it, but you might like. The problem was it took me several tries to change it and it should not be that hard to change.

So even with those two minor faults, this is still a great Saber for the price. As someone who was 10 years old when Star Wars came out, even now holding this and turning it on makes me smile.

"May the Force be with You"

text_fidelity_a:
Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions Well first I have to admit, I do not have an internet saavy family. And this game is very much tied into internet memes from "I can haz cheezburgers?" to "Erhmahgerd." Luckily, I have spent a healthy amount of my life researching internet culture, but I ended up having to explain a lot of the cards to my kids.

But the reason I love this game is because of how engaged it kept the kids, and the amount of laughs that it produced. The selfies were ridiculous and caused laughter in itself and the cards played were even better. The game is pretty simple, pick a card from your hand to recreate in a selfie, then others play cards with scenarios that best fit your selfie. There are a lot of "Trying not to poop" type of cards so the humor is a little juvenile but perfect for keeping kids engaged.

Everyone willingly took their turns on the cell phone and everyone seemed to really enjoy the game. Scoring was pretty meaningless which was good. I was thinking that since the person taking the photo got to be the judge of who gets the point for the best caption that there would be hurt feelings and poorly awarded points, but the fun of the selfies and reading the cards trumped any controversy. Actually we ended without caring who scored points.

All in all this is a great ice breaking game.
text_fidelity_b: Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions

My mom tells the story that I would pull it out to bake and she was like...Oh gosh, there she goes again. Party Fun Activity/Gift for, Teens Boys and Girls I got this kit for our family for Christmas. My daughter was so excited! We started making things right away. text_fidelity_a: WEQIN Water Guns for Kids Adults 1200CC Squirt Guns High 3 Nozzles Capacity Water Blaster Water Toys Summer Gun Toys Water Shooter Fighting Games Play Toys… This is a great way to cool off in the heat with the kids! My little ones loved how easy it was to replenish after using up the tank (the entire back opens up so it fills much faster), and the triple-nozzle front was a blast (literally! ha). One thing I didn't realize beforehand, however, is that it works entirely by pump action. That is, unlike a super soaker or other water pistol that builds pressure with the pump and then releases with a trigger, the pump is the entire firing mechanism, and the "trigger" is just for show (doesn't do anything). Pulling back on the pump fires the water, and the strength is adjusted  by how hard/fast you pull back. My older kids were able to figure that out, but my youngest (3 years old) found it disappointing. He likes the trigger kind because it is easy for him to fire, and with this he wasn't able to figure out the dexterity to make it shoot very far. For what it is, it works and is fun, but I do sort of wish it had a trigger that wasn't just there for looks.
text_fidelity_b: WEQIN Water Guns for Kids Adults 1200CC Squirt Guns High 3 Nozzles Capacity Water Blaster Water Toys Summer Gun Toys Water Shooter Fighting Games Play Toys…

VTech Go! Go! Smart Wheels Race & Play Adventure Park 5 stars for the toy itself. 0 stars for the directions - they are awful! The pictures are in blurry black and white, and the wording is confusing. It took me far too long to put together, but I was impressed by the finished product.

First of all - this is big! Look carefully at the specs on this toy to see if it will fit well (or dominate) your play space. The colors and designs are bright and cheerful, which I like. There are a few specific mechanical steps to make this work right with the car, and I worried that it would be too complicated for my 2yo granddaughter. (1) The arm needs to be clicked down into position, (2) you need to wind the car up the ramp (and the crank for that is tricky - if you let go just a little, it slides back to the bottom), then once the car slides down the ramp into the cradle you need to (3) release the arm for the catapult to launch down the second slide. Again - sounds complicated, right? But my granddaughter mastered it in no time! I was surprised and happy about that.

I was also very happy that she played with this over and over. She never seemed to get bored with it. The little car plays music and phrases as it goes along, and even when all the steps didn't go perfectly (ie: the car crashed), my granddaughter was amused. One quick note: some of the joints seem to come apart easily, and since toddlers are a little rough, we needed to keep an eye on this. Still, this will be a great toy that grows with our grandkids!
text_fidelity_b: VTech Go! Go! Smart Wheels Race & Play Adventure Park
